assessment.summary: JAK2 is an exceptionally well-validated drug target with 171 PDB structures (best resolution 1.3Å), over 19,000 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and 12 approved drugs including ruxolitinib, fedratinib, baricitinib, and pacritinib. The target has extensive structural, chemical, and clinical validation across multiple disease indications including myeloproliferative neoplasms and inflammatory conditions. Druggability is unambiguously high by every metric.
evidence_gaps: Selectivity over other JAK family members (JAK1, JAK3, TYK2) remains a challenge for next-generation inhibitors
Covalent or allosteric inhibitor approaches are less explored relative to ATP-competitive scaffolds
Structural data for JAK2 in complex with non-kinase domain binding ligands or PROTAC degraders is limited
Resistance mechanisms (e.g., JAK2 mutations conferring inhibitor resistance) are not fully characterised structurally
Disease-specific contexts (e.g., solid tumours vs. haematological malignancies) may require distinct targeting strategies not fully addressed by existing literature
